title: A Benchmark for Electrical Load Forecasting Across Grid Levels (arXiv 2607.15705), abstract page
note: Abstract page, v1 submitted 17 Jul 2026, cs.LG, CC BY 4.0. Headline: on three load datasets (a TSO control area, low-voltage feeders, end consumers) Transformer-based methods beat established ones by 6.6 to 10.7% in forecast error; a plain Transformer beats the authors' modified YAformer; Chronos-2 is competitive zero-shot on two datasets and misses special events on the TSO series.

title: A Benchmark for Electrical Load Forecasting Across Grid Levels (arXiv 2607.15705), full text
note: Design: hourly load, 96-hour horizon, a forecast issued every hour. TransnetBW (1 series, ENTSO-E, 2015-2025; test 2024-2025), FeederBW (200 feeders; test Apr 2024 to Mar 2025), Electricity-287 (287 UCI clients; test 8 Aug to 31 Dec 2014). Ten methods plus a same-day-type persistence baseline; 100 Bayesian HPO trials each; monthly retraining on the two longer sets, static split on the third.

title: A Benchmark for Electrical Load Forecasting Across Grid Levels (arXiv 2607.15705), full text
note: Covariates: TransnetBW gets ERA5 reanalysis temperature, irradiance, precipitation, 10 m wind and a holiday flag; FeederBW gets short-term weather forecasts by post code plus holiday; Electricity-287 gets ERA5 for Portugal. Trained models also get hour, weekday and month encodings. The authors say this weather would not be available at forecast time and that errors may be unrealistically low.

title: A Benchmark for Electrical Load Forecasting Across Grid Levels (arXiv 2607.15705), full text
note: Headline numbers in the text: best Transformer-family model is 8.3% (TransnetBW), 6.6% (FeederBW) and 10.7% (Electricity-287) below the best non-Transformer model, named as CNN, LSTM and N-HITS. Best model vs persistence baseline: 59.6%, 42.3%, 23.3% lower error. The plain Transformer is best on TransnetBW and FeederBW; Chronos-2 is best on Electricity-287.

title: A Benchmark for Electrical Load Forecasting Across Grid Levels (arXiv 2607.15705), full text
note: Chronos-2: second on FeederBW, best on Electricity-287, far behind on TransnetBW with large errors around holidays, long weekends and Christmas. Extra long-weekend and school-holiday flags bring its TransnetBW MAE to 180 MW, still behind the trained deep models. The paper states Electricity-287's training set is in Chronos-2's pretraining data, so that result is not zero-shot.

title: A Benchmark for Electrical Load Forecasting Across Grid Levels (arXiv 2607.15705), full text
note: By horizon: Chronos-2 leads at short leads (hours 2 to 6 on TransnetBW, first 6 h on FeederBW, first 31 h on Electricity-287); the trained Transformer's error grows less and it leads at long leads. Discussion: Chronos-2 is weak on rare events and longer horizons. LightGBM is best only at one step ahead on TransnetBW.

title: A Benchmark for Electrical Load Forecasting Across Grid Levels (arXiv 2607.15705), full text
note: Significance: per-series Diebold-Mariano tests at 5% on horizon-averaged absolute error per origin. TransnetBW: Transformer and YAformer not different, both ahead of all others. FeederBW: Transformer ahead of Chronos-2 on 46% of series, behind on 20%. Electricity-287: Transformer ahead on 39%, Chronos-2 on 14%. No intervals on the error figures; no seed spread reported.

title: A Benchmark for Electrical Load Forecasting Across Grid Levels (arXiv 2607.15705), full text
note: Ablations (figures only, no numbers in text): removing covariates hurts both the Transformer and Chronos-2 on all three sets; monthly retraining beats one training a year; Chronos-2 with one week of context barely beats the baseline, a month is close to the 8192-step maximum. Runtime on an A100 GPU: Transformer training 11 min 40 s per model on TransnetBW; Chronos-2 78 ms per forecast.

title: A Benchmark for Electrical Load Forecasting Across Grid Levels (arXiv 2607.15705), full text
note: Availability: the text says code, preprocessed data and the predictions of all models are public at github.com/KIT-IAI/load-forecasting-benchmark. title: A Benchmark for Electrical Load Forecasting Across Grid Levels (arXiv 2607.15705), PDF
note: Our arithmetic on Table 4: 143.6 vs 156.5 is 8.2% and 3.18 vs 3.41 is 6.7%, matching the text within rounding. On Electricity-287 the table has LightGBM (8.86) ahead of N-HITS (8.92) on nMAE, and no pair gives exactly 10.7%: Transformer vs N-HITS 10.4%, Chronos-2 vs LightGBM 10.6%, Chronos-2 vs N-HITS 11.2%. Which pair the text used is not stated.

title: KIT-IAI/load-forecasting-benchmark (README)
note: Authors' repository. README: Python 3.11 with uv, preprocessing scripts for the three datasets, main.py driven by config files, logging to Weights and Biases. Preprocessed Electricity and FeederBW data, ERA5 weather and the best models' predictions are on a KIT file share, not in the repository; TransnetBW load is downloaded by the user from ENTSO-E. N-HITS and TFT are adapted from neuralforecast.

title: research: primary sources for and against the claim
note: One standard-tier call, LinkedIn excluded, 9 sources.
